checks.upstream_claim: 95c5386ddb8a '[RISCV][NFCI] Rationalize Immediate Definitions (#120718)' is an ancestor of llvmorg-20.1.8 and not of llvmorg-19.1.7. It adds EncoderMethod=getImmOpValue and a constant-only MCOperandPredicate to class RISCVUImmOp, which uimm5 (RISCVUImmLeafOp<5>) inherits. At llvmorg-19.1.7 uimm5 had no EncoderMethod, so it used the default getMachineOpValue, where the fork hunk (RISCVMCCodeEmitter.cpp:388-410) emits fixup_pulpv2_loop_setupi for LOOP*setupi. The claim is accurate.
checks.pattern: uimm5pcrel has the same fields as 19.1.7's uimm5: ParserMatchClass UImmAsmOperand<5>, DecoderMethod decodeUImmOperand<5>, OperandType OPERAND_UIMM5, OperandNamespace RISCVOp, 5-bit ImmLeaf, no EncoderMethod, no MCOperandPredicate. It differs from the fork's uimm12pcrel only by also keeping OperandType/Namespace, which 19's uimm5 had, so verifier behaviour is unchanged. Upstream's own vendor label operand (cv.beqimm/cv.bneimm use simm13_lsb0 at RISCVInstrInfoXCV.td:505-510 and RISCVInstrInfo.td:271, llvmorg-20.1.8) is a dedicated label operand, not a generic constant-only uimmN/simmN, so the fix follows upstream's approach. It reuses the fork's existing fixup path instead of adding a new encoder, which is the minimal change. Only LOOP0setupi/LOOP1setupi change.
checks.left_behind: All fork instructions that the fork's getMachineOpValue expression hunk handles (LOOP{0,1}{setup,setupi,starti,endi,counti}) now take labels through uimm12pcrel/uimm5pcrel, which are plain Operands with the default encoder. The only other fork uses of uimm5 are LOOP0count/LOOP1count ($uimmS), which never carry a label and are never built in C++ (grep finds no LOOP[01]count in lib/Target/RISCV/*.cpp). Fork branch-like operands: P_BEQIMM/P_BNEIMM use upstream simm13_lsb0 (unchanged by 95c5386ddb8a in any way that matters); uimm13_lsb0 and uimm6_lsb0_pulp are fork Operand<OtherVT> with their own encoders. The fork .td files Xdma/Xfrep/Xsmallfloat/Xssr have no label operands. Nothing is left behind.

Compiled with toolchains/port-19/bin/clang and build/20-R001/bin/clang (flags from the task), then compared llvm-objdump -dr, readelf -rW and readelf -x .text. (a) Reproducer lp_setupi_mc_crash.c: identical. lp.setupi x0, 0x3e8, 0x6 = 3e83507b, no relocations. (b) Same with -pulp-loop-range-immediate=0 (lp.starti/lp.endi/lp.counti): identical. (c) s1.c, 4 functions: lp.setupi with counts 100/31/2000 and end offsets 0x6/0x17/0x1b (different loop sizes), plus lp.setup: identical. I also checked by hand that the end offset at 0x48 (0x17 -> 0x76) points to the last instruction of the loop body. (d) Loop level x1: clang cannot produce nested hardware loops (see other findings), so I stopped llc after pulp-hwloops, renamed LOOP0*->LOOP1* in the MIR, and emitted objects with -start-after=pulp-hwloops on each toolchain. v0 and s1: identical (lp.setupi x1 = ...50fb, same offsets, no relocations). (e) w2/w3 (lp.setup, lp.starti/endi/counti forms): identical. The other variants (v1, v3, v4, w1) differ only through unrelated LLVM 19->20 codegen changes (register allocation, scheduling). No relocation difference appears anywhere. port-20 (unfixed) still asserts at RISCVMCCodeEmitter.cpp:555 on s1.c, which confirms the before state.

other_findings_not_blocking: Pre-existing, also in port-19: a SIGSEGV in the 'PULP Hardware Loops' pass on nested constant-trip-count loops (e.g. for i<10 { for j<20 ... }), on runtime-trip-count pure-arithmetic loops, and on some single loops (for i<31 {x=x*3+(y>>5); y^=x; cnt++;}). This means clang cannot currently produce an x1-level hardware loop from C. Same root family as benchmarks/gap9-sweep/sim/repro/hwloop_var_tripcount_crash.c. Not a step-20 regression. The conductor may want a separate task.

The worker's proposed test (object output of lp.setupi at both loop levels, checked by encoding) is appropriate. It should include an x1 case, e.g. a MIR-based llc -start-after=pulp-hwloops -filetype=obj test, because C/IR cannot reach x1 while the nested-loop crash exists.
